name: Notion
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Notion MCP → All MCP clients
gotcha_copy: Notion has one combined grant with no read/write split. Reauthorization is required after 180 days or 30 days of inactivity. The grant is listed under Settings then Notion MCP, as an MCP client named "kiro" or after the loopback redirect URL the runtime registered (for example 127.0.0.1:5xxxx) rather than Kiro Crew; the Connections page lists workspace apps such as Zapier and never shows it.
revoke_verified_note: user click-verified: grants appear ONLY on Settings → Notion MCP → All MCP clients, a settings-modal page with no dedicated URL, so the link points at the workspace home instead of a deep link that cannot be addressed. www.notion.so is NOT that home -- it redirects a logged-in user to the notion.com marketing site; app.notion.com lands on the workspace, where the manual path applies

name: GitHub
gotcha_copy: GitHub needs a one-time Kiro app registration, and the loopback callback must exactly match the registered URI. Scopes are coarse; prefer the read-only server variant.

name: Linear
gotcha_copy: Linear separates read and write access; Kiro Crew installs the dedicated read-only /mcp/readonly endpoint. Use the MCP Servers tab for write access.

name: Atlassian
prerequisite_copy: Requires an Atlassian account with a Jira or Confluence site — without one, the consent page's Accept button stays disabled.
gotcha_copy: Covers Jira and Confluence, not Trello. The default grant includes write access; use Edit permissions on Atlassian's consent page to trim it.

name: Stripe
gotcha_copy: Read and write access is controlled at the tool level, not by OAuth scopes. The server is in public preview; use test mode first.

name: Vercel
gotcha_copy: Vercel uses PKCE, refresh, and provider-side revocation. Review the selected team before approving access.

name: GitLab
prerequisite_copy: Enable GitLab Duo with beta and experimental features, and allow MCP server access for your top-level group — without them, connecting succeeds but exposes no tools.
gotcha_copy: GitLab offers a single mcp scope with no read-only variant, so this grant can write: the same token that reads issues can open issues and merge requests, comment, and run or delete pipelines.

name: Superhuman Mail
prerequisite_copy: Requires a Superhuman Mail Business or Enterprise plan — on other plans the consent page refuses the connection.
gotcha_copy: One combined grant with no read-only variant: the same token that lists threads can send mail from your account (send_draft, with a default one-minute undo window), trash threads and edit calendar events, so ask for drafts and review them in Superhuman before sending.
revoke_verified_note: UNVERIFIED: no Business-plan account was available, so the link points at the setup article rather than a settings deep link. Launch-gated until a logged-in check records the surface that lists MCP client grants and refreshes this date.

name: Sentry
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Account → API → Authorized Applications → Revoke
gotcha_copy: The consent screen grants skills, not scopes: approve only 'inspect' and 'docs' for read-only use; 'triage' and 'project-management' unlock writes (update_issue, create_project, delete_uptime_monitor) and analyze_issue_with_seer starts a billable Seer run. The grant is locked to the single organization picked at login. The tool set changes with org/project scoping and granted skills, so read tools/list rather than assuming.

name: Supabase
revoke_manual_path: Dashboard → Organization settings → OAuth Apps → Authorized apps → Revoke
gotcha_copy: The grant is per organization and only an organization owner can approve it, so pick the org that owns your project at login. Kiro Crew installs the documented ?read_only=true variant, which runs SQL as a read-only Postgres role and drops the mutating tools (apply_migration, deploy_edge_function, create_project); use the MCP Servers tab for the writable endpoint. No client-selectable scopes: consent is all-or-nothing at the org level.

name: Airtable
revoke_manual_path: Avatar → Integrations → Third-party integrations → select the integration → Delete integration
prerequisite_copy: Enterprise Scale workspaces can block third-party MCP clients; ask an Airtable admin to allow-list this client under Admin Panel → Integrations & development.
gotcha_copy: There is no read-only endpoint: read-only is achieved only by declining the data.records:write and schema.bases:write scopes at consent, and the server otherwise mirrors your Airtable role. Base access is chosen during OAuth (all bases or a custom set), so a base missing from list_bases usually means it was not granted. Refresh tokens expire after 60 idle days and public API limits (5 req/s per base) apply.

name: PayPal
revoke_manual_path: Log in → Third Party API users → Actions (⋯) → Delete
prerequisite_copy: The live server needs a PayPal Business account; test with a Developer account against https://mcp.sandbox.paypal.com/mcp first.
gotcha_copy: This server moves real money on the live endpoint: create_refund, pay_order, checkout_cart, send_invoice and accept_dispute_claim execute immediately with no PayPal-side confirmation, and the consent screen only shows openid/email/profile so it does not reveal that capability. Treat every tool starting with create_, send_, pay_, cancel_, update_, accept_ or checkout_ as a write. Prefer the sandbox endpoint until the flow is trusted.

name: Asana
revoke_manual_path: Profile photo → My Settings → Apps → Authorized Apps → Deauthorize
prerequisite_copy: Asana does not support dynamic client registration: Kiro needs a one-time MCP app registration in the Asana developer console before Connect can work.
gotcha_copy: Authorization grants every tool at the user's own permission level: there are no scopes (the only accepted value is 'default') and no read-only mode, and delete_task is permanent. Access tokens last one hour and are bound to the single workspace chosen at consent. The v1 /sse endpoint is deprecated; only /v2/mcp is supported. Like GitHub, this entry stays gated until the Kiro app registration lands and client_id is set.

name: Figma
revoke_manual_path: Account menu → Settings → Security → Connect apps → Revoke access
prerequisite_copy: Figma only accepts OAuth clients listed in its MCP Catalog; Kiro must be admitted from Figma's client waitlist before Connect can succeed.
gotcha_copy: One grant covers read and write tools: use_figma, create_new_file, upload_assets, generate_diagram and the create_*/update_* tools modify files (a Dev seat is read-only outside drafts; a Full seat edits any file you can edit). Read tools count against a 200/day quota (Enterprise 600/day); View and Collab seats get only 6–20 calls a month. Vendor approval pending: Figma admits clients from a waitlist, so this entry cannot pass the launch gate until Kiro is listed.

name: Canva
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Connected apps → Disconnect
prerequisite_copy: Canva must allow-list the OAuth redirect URI before sign-in works; Kiro applies through the waitlist form on the Canva MCP docs page.
gotcha_copy: One grant covers every tool: generate-design (spends Canva AI credits), editing transactions, export-design, upload-asset-from-url, comment-on-design and the folder tools create or modify content; edit-class tools only succeed on designs you can already edit. Each user signs in with their own account; there is no org-level auth. Vendor approval pending: the redirect-URI allowlist is granted per client, so this entry cannot pass the launch gate until Canva admits Kiro.

name: Dropbox
revoke_manual_path: Avatar → Settings → Apps → arrow next to the app → Disconnect
prerequisite_copy: Dropbox admits dynamic registration only for clients on its trusted list; other clients must first register a Dropbox app and connect with its key.
gotcha_copy: Beta server whose grant includes write scopes: Delete, Move, Copy, CreateFile, CreateSharedLink and RestoreFolder change or share your files (Delete is recoverable from Deleted files). Tool names are PascalCase (WhoAmI, ListFolder). Vendor approval pending: dynamic client registration is honoured only for Dropbox's trusted-client list, so this entry cannot pass the launch gate until Kiro is on it or a Dropbox app is registered.

name: Miro
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Team settings → Apps & Integrations → select the MCP client → Uninstall for me
prerequisite_copy: On Enterprise plans the MCP server is off by default: a Company Admin must enable it under Admin settings → Apps & Integrations → MCP and, when access control is set to specific clients, allow-list this client.
gotcha_copy: The grant is bound to the single Miro team picked at login and is last-one-wins: authorizing another team or another MCP client drops the previous connection. The server advertises a boards:read scope but the consent screen does not let you drop boards:write, so treat every connection as read-write: board_create, canvas_create_from_svg and canvas_update_from_svg (which also deletes items), code_widget_delete, comment_reply, comment_resolve, image_create and prototype_create all change boards, and context_get spends Miro AI credits. Every call counts against a daily per-plan quota.

name: Webflow
revoke_manual_path: Workspace settings → Apps & Integrations → Connected Apps → select the MCP client → Remove
prerequisite_copy: Only site owners and admins can authorize the MCP server for a site; other members see those sites greyed out on the consent page.
gotcha_copy: Each authorization is locked to one workspace and to the sites ticked at consent; switching workspaces means removing and re-adding the connection. There is no read-only mode: access is granted per tool and every data_*_tool bundles its read and write actions, so publish_site, publish_collection_items, delete_collection_items, delete_asset, delete_font, delete_form_submission, delete_registered_script (irreversible), delete_branch, remove_element and the custom-code, robots.txt and redirect writers are all reachable. The server also installs its MCP Bridge App on every authorized site. The agent can do exactly what your Webflow role allows.

name: Netlify
revoke_manual_path: User settings → Applications → Authorized applications → Revoke
gotcha_copy: The server advertises read and write scopes, but its OAuth broker exchanges either for a full Netlify user token and does not filter tools by scope, so a read grant still exposes every write tool: netlify-project-services-updater (create-new-project, manage-project-env-vars, update-visitor-access-controls, manage-form-submissions), netlify-extension-services-updater (change-extension-installation, initialize-database, which can provision paid add-ons) and netlify-deploy-services-updater. Read-only use means calling only the *-services-reader tools. The grant covers every team your Netlify user belongs to, not one team.

name: Amplitude
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Organization settings → Content Access → MCP (org admin; blocks the server for the whole organization)
prerequisite_copy: Be logged in to exactly one Amplitude organization when you authorize; multiple logins break the OAuth flow. Org admins can block the server under Settings → Content Access → MCP, and the Use MCP (read) and Use MCP (write) role actions gate calls per project. EU-resident data uses https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com/mcp instead.
gotcha_copy: Kiro Crew asks for the mcp:read scope only; mcp:write unlocks the writing tools: use_amp_dashboards, use_amp_notebooks, use_amp_comments, share_amp_entities, create_experiment, update_experiment, create_metric, create_flags, update_flag, create_properties, update_properties, manage_amp_events (can delete events), manage_amp_data_taxonomy (merges and deletes tracking-plan branches) and use_amplitude_cohorts, which can also sync cohort data out to Braze, Iterable, S3 or a webhook. There is no per-tool consent screen: your Amplitude role decides, and denied tools stay visible in tools/list and fail only when called. Amplitude documents no per-user page that lists MCP grants; revocation is the org-level MCP block or removing the role actions.

name: Mixpanel
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Organization → Overview → MCP toggle (org admin; disables MCP for the whole organization, takes up to 15 minutes)
prerequisite_copy: An organization admin must switch MCP on under Settings → Organization → Overview before anyone can connect; the change takes up to 15 minutes. Mixpanel states the MCP server is not covered by its HIPAA BAA. EU and IN projects use https://mcp-eu.mixpanel.com/mcp or https://mcp-in.mixpanel.com/mcp.
gotcha_copy: The OAuth scopes are all analysis-flavoured (projects, events, insights, funnels) and there is no separate write scope to leave out, so the connection can read and write; only your Mixpanel role and project permissions limit it. Writing tools include Create-Dashboard, Update-Dashboard, Delete-Dashboard, Edit-Event, Edit-Property, Bulk-Edit-Events, Bulk-Edit-Properties, Create-Tag, Delete-Tag, Dismiss-Issues, Update-Business-Context, Merge-Group, Create-Cohort, Update-Cohort, Delete-Cohort, Create-Lookup-Table, Create-Metric, Update-Metric, Create-Experiment, Update-Experiment, Create-Feature-Flag and Update-Feature-Flag. Kiro Crew requests only the ten mandatory scopes, the narrowest documented option. Mixpanel documents no per-user page listing MCP grants; the org-level MCP switch is the only vendor-side revocation.

name: Cloudflare
revoke_manual_path: Profile → Access Management → Connected Applications → Revoke
gotcha_copy: This is Cloudflare's Workers Bindings server, one of several separate Cloudflare MCP hosts, each with its own OAuth grant. The consent screen has no read-only option: the server always requests workers:write and d1:write, and its tools include hard deletes (kv_namespace_delete, r2_bucket_delete, d1_database_delete, hyperdrive_config_delete), creates, and d1_database_query, which runs arbitrary SQL including writes against billable D1. Limit the blast radius by ticking only the accounts you need on the consent screen; when the grant spans several accounts every tool needs an account_id argument or it errors. Use the MCP Servers tab for the read-only observability host.

name: Hugging Face
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Connected Applications → find the MCP client → Revoke
gotcha_copy: The plain server URL answers without a login, giving anonymous read-only browsing of public models, datasets, Spaces, papers and docs (hub_repo_search, hub_repo_details, hf_fs); Kiro Crew installs the ?login variant so the server demands your account and a successful connection means a real grant. Signing in switches the tool list to what you enabled at huggingface.co/settings/mcp and can add hf_jobs (runs paid compute), hf_sandbox, hf_sandbox_exec and hf_sandbox_fs (cloud sandboxes), create_repo and hf_fs_write (writes files and opens pull requests) plus any Gradio Space tools you picked, which spend Space or inference quota. Keep to the read-mcp scope for read-only use; jobs, contribute-repos and inference-api are the scopes that spend or write.

name: Zapier
revoke_manual_path: mcp.zapier.com → select the server named after this client → Edit access → Remove, or delete the server
gotcha_copy: Zapier creates one MCP server per connecting client, named after the client, and auto-provisions tools from the apps already connected to your own Zapier account, so the tool list is per-user and grows as the agent enables actions. Every successful execute_zapier_read_action or execute_zapier_write_action call spends two tasks from your Zapier plan; execute_zapier_write_action, enable_zapier_action, disable_zapier_action, auto_provision_mcp, create_zapier_skill, update_zapier_skill, delete_zapier_skill and write_code_action change state in Zapier or in your connected apps. For a fixed read-only surface, switch the server to manual configuration at mcp.zapier.com and add only search and read actions; the agent then cannot enable new ones. The OAuth scopes are identity-only and do not narrow tool access.

name: Square
revoke_manual_path: Square Dashboard → Settings → App integrations → (•••) next to the app → Disconnect App
prerequisite_copy: Square keeps an allowlist of MCP clients and refuses registration from any other client; Kiro must be admitted through a request in the Square developer forum before Connect can work. The remote server reaches production data only; there is no Sandbox mode for the hosted server.
gotcha_copy: The server exposes three tools: get_service_info and get_type_info only read API metadata, but make_api_request executes any Square API call, including payments, refunds, payouts, invoices, gift cards and deleting catalog items, customers or team members, against your live production account. Read-only is enforced only by the permissions you tick on the consent screen (choose *_READ permissions only); the DISALLOW_WRITES switch exists solely for the local server. The grant is bound to the single Square merchant account you log in with. Vendor approval pending: Square admits MCP clients from an allowlist, so this entry cannot pass the launch gate until Kiro is listed.

name: Postman
revoke_manual_path: Avatar → Settings → Active sessions → Revoke (Postman documents no dedicated authorized-apps page)
gotcha_copy: Postman serves several endpoints on the same host; Kiro Crew installs /minimal (about 40 tools, the vendor default) rather than /mcp (Full, 100+ tools including deleteWorkspace, deleteCollection, deleteEnvironment, deleteMock, deleteMonitor, deleteSpec and transferWorkspaceToTeam). There is no read-only mode and no scope picker at consent: the token acts as you across every workspace you can access, and even /minimal includes write tools (createWorkspace, createCollection, putCollection, putEnvironment, updateMock, publishMock, runCollection, syncCollectionWithSpec). Use the MCP Servers tab for the Full endpoint. The remote server sends anonymous telemetry by default.

name: Neon
revoke_manual_path: Neon Console → avatar → Account settings (Neon documents no authorized-apps list; the server's own revocation endpoint is the certain path)
gotcha_copy: Kiro Crew installs the documented ?readonly=true variant, which keeps the read tools (about half of the set; run_sql still executes SELECT statements against your live databases) and drops the writers even if Full access is granted at consent. The writable endpoint can delete_project, delete_branch, delete_postgres_database, reset_from_parent, restore_snapshot, delete_storage_bucket and delete_storage_objects_by_prefix, and create_project or create_postgres_endpoint start billable compute; use the MCP Servers tab for it. The grant covers every organization and project your account can see unless you add ?projectId=. Neon states MCP is for development only, never production databases.

name: Prisma
revoke_manual_path: Prisma Console → select the workspace → Integrations → find the application → Revoke
gotcha_copy: There is no read-only scope: the only functional scope is workspace:admin, so the token can do everything you can in the chosen workspace. Read tools are fetch_workspace_details, list_prisma_postgres_databases, list_prisma_postgres_connection_strings (returns live credentials), list_prisma_postgres_backups, introspect_database_schema, list_object_store_buckets and search_prisma_documentation; the rest write or destroy: create_prisma_postgres_database and create_prisma_postgres_recovery provision billable databases, execute_sql_query and execute_prisma_postgres_schema_update run arbitrary SQL and DDL, and delete_prisma_postgres_database, delete_prisma_postgres_connection_string, delete_object_store_bucket (wipes all objects and keys) and delete_object_store_bucket_key are irreversible. The consent screen binds the grant to one Prisma workspace picked at login.
